about: The country workshops (Docs/Design/72-pulling-the-country-into-the-world.md, 4.6 and the Siting's Phase 5 rows; doc 71, 5): real businesses in the communities, each at the map's fixed building id (`building`, an interior; its keeper's flat `<building>_flat`, or the community's flat `for` its name), merged into its community's market (communities.json: the map's entry for the building gives its work spots, else `work` here). Their posts are staffed as the communities' markets are (farm_people.json `market`: the keeper of the towns' trades and shops, then those who keep the house, then service and labour, the post's words first; the hands of those who keep the house first), when the community's first farm or works is, the keeper living in the flat, the hands in the community's cottages; nobody is made. Each is a business of businesses.json (`business`: its crafts in crafts.json, its wares what they make) with a till of its own, its posts paid as a city maker's are (the till's keeper's and hands' wages, which follow its takings: the rule wageDrift), and owned by `house` (doc 42, Phase 5b: a workshop is a House's, which takes all the profit): what its till holds each night over its float and floatWagesDays of its wages goes to that House's estate (the Country's purse, the Houses' estates and the sea trade, booked by House with the works' rents). The House is the land's: Coldwater's and Larkfield's the Crown's (its herds' and grain farms'), the potteries Greatly's (by its clay pits: House Greatly is construction, doc 67 R25), Oakhaven's Timberland's (the woods'). They sell to the city's shops till to till (country.json `suppliers`, the resale path: at the store room's price, no toll, no carriage) and to any household whose own community's shops lack their goods; the store room supplies only what they lack. Crews sized to their inputs and to what the Country sold of their goods in country4's year 3 (the doc's ~29 was doc 71's plausible count before the inputs were known). A world without a building (build 60's export) has none of its workshop: its goods stay the store room's.

workshops.name: Coldwater Soapworks
workshops.about: Fine soap and tallow candles of the herds' tallow, herbs from the marsh, cord from the chandlery and the ropewalk: candles ~16 crew-hours a day, soap ~64 for the ~31 a day the general stores sell (the Country sold ~26 of them in country5b's year 3, the soapworks' herbs and hours short).

workshops.name: Coldwater Looms
workshops.about: Wool scarves of the two sheep runs' wool: ~43 a day (the ~28 the Country still sold the rag-and-bone men in country5b's year 3 among them), ~67 crew-hours.

workshops.name: Larkfield Looms
workshops.about: Linen of the grain farms' flax (the presses', the tailors' and the apothecaries'), and linen neckerchiefs beside the tailor's (~10 a day short in country5b's year 3): ~60 crew-hours a day (the neckerchiefs first, and the linen they left short).

workshops.name: Larkfield Print House
workshops.about: Pamphlets and paper (the Country sold ~19 pamphlets and ~4 paper a day): with Oakhaven's, ~60 crew-hours a day; since country5b's carry-overs a third hand at each, for the ~8 pamphlets a day the Country still sold the general stores.

workshops.name: Larkfield Smithy
workshops.about: Iron hoops (beside the smithies and the cooperage), nails and cookpots, of the Country's iron bars, for the farms' baskets first: the smith and a striker (the farms' ~85p a day of them; alone, the hoops took every hour and no nails were made: a smith alone now saves its hours for the nails once they are sold out). The striker's label names no business (a hand's never does, and any with the workshop's name would be the city smithy's).

workshops.name: Fenshore Kilns
workshops.about: Clay pots of the Mirebridge pit's clay: the potter and a kiln hand for the ~42 pots a day the two potteries and the rag-and-bone men sell (~34 crew-hours; the Country sold ~18 in country5b's year 3).

workshops.name: Southmeadow Kilns
workshops.about: Clay pots of the Fens pit's clay, the potter and a kiln hand.

workshops.name: Oakhaven Print House
workshops.about: Pamphlets and paper, the press nearer the city (a third hand, as Larkfield's).

workshops.name: Coldwater Still
workshops.about: Apple brandy and brandy (doc 72, Progress, "The producers and the fixes"; the user, 2026-11-04: new producers for them): House Fell's, whose land the orchards and vines are (doc 67: Fell wine and fruit), in the village of the Greenholt's two orchards, where the apples piled ~9 a day an orchard in iron6's year 3. Cider pressed of the orchards' apples (2 a jug) and stilled into apple brandy (3 jugs a bottle), the vineyards' wine into brandy (2 bottles to 1). No household bought either before (the distillery's sat unsold); now a comfort, so sized small: ~5 apple brandy and ~1 brandy a day, ~24 crew-hours (the stillmaster and a hand).
